_comment: The core technique catalogue of the disinformation lens (tools/platform-plan.md, the core-versus-pack table), in its shipped form. Each criterion is a general technique attributed to the person or text that stated it, with that public source and its date; subject nouns are parameters ({name} in the statement) that a lens instance fills (packs/<pack>/lenses/<instance>.json). An instance names the criteria it draws on and keeps the project's own references to where it holds each statement. The catalogue is the form of the lens, not a judgement of any source.
public_attributions: UFO Secrets Are Held By A Global Cabal

criterion_fields: source (kind, name, public: the public interview or document, venue or publisher, date, address or section; catalogued). The private references to where a project holds the statement (a note, its rows, a time) live in the pack's lens instance under catalogue_refs, never here

roles.technique: what the source says the adversary does; testable only against ground truth
roles.operative: a rule the source uses to sort sources; the filter uses these
roles.exculpatory: why honest people get it wrong

sides.disclosure: the side the source treats as truthful
sides.control: the side the source treats as serving secrecy or an organisation behind it
sides.unwitting: honest but uninformed, intercepted or gaslit; weighted only for what they saw themselves
sides.mixed: placed on both sides at different times

instance_fields: sides (the source's own words for the five sides)
criteria (subject-content criteria, same fields as the catalogue's plus statement filled)
qualifications (criterion id: the source's own qualification)
catalogue_criteria (the catalogue criteria this instance draws on)
catalogue_refs (criterion id: the project's private reference to the statement)

weighting_rules: discount: the row's Speaker is placed on the control side (one strike; the poison pill is inside the true coating)
discount: the row's first chain segment names a control-side person as a hop other than the speaker (the row rests on a known co-mingler)
weight: the row's Speaker is placed on the disclosure side
weight: the row's Speaker is placed unwitting and the row is firsthand (the truth as they know it, for what they saw)
weight: the row's first chain segment names a disclosure-side person and no control-side person
unplaced: everything else, including unwitting speakers' non-firsthand rows, mixed and undecided speakers, and speakers the source never names

T1.test: control-side people whose own claims the cross-check tables record as corroborated by an independent route not itself placed control; each is a counterexample to the sorting

T2.test: rows in which a speaker or origin denies the subject's central possession claim; a disclosure-side denier is a counterexample (the criteria are the instance's)

T3.test: rows presenting the subject's agents as hostile, harmful or a threat; a disclosure-side speaker is a counterexample

T4.test: the one-strike rule applied to the source's own sourcing: relations and rows that rest on control-side people

T5.test: firsthand reports of threats or reprisals against placed speakers; a control-side report is a counterexample

T6.test: disclosure- or unwitting-side people recorded approaching the source's camp as adversaries or red-teamers
